title: Crown graphs maximise the representation number of bipartite graphs
summary: The representation number of a graph is the least positive integer $k$ for which its vertices can be arranged in a word, each occurring $k$ times, so that two distinct letters alternate precisely when the corresponding vertices are adjacent. We prove that every bipartite graph on $N\ge9$ vertices has representation number at most $\lceil N/4\rceil$. Together with the known representation number of crown graphs, this settles the conjecture that crowns maximise the representation number among bipartite graphs of the same order.
